 TRADE: Eagles Trading OLB Arnold Ebiketie To Bengals
 By Logan Ulrich - November 10, 2026 
 According to Ian Rapoport , the Eagles are trading OLB Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
 Cincinnati makes a cheap move to add some edge-rushing depth as they look to fortify a potential Super Bowl window.
 The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. points out the Bengals eyed Ebiketie as a free agent target in the spring. With second-round OLB Cashius Howell on injured reserve with a wrist injury, it made sense to circle back.  
 Meanwhile the Eagles keep adding draft capital, this time a low-level move for a veteran on an expiring contract. 
 Ebiketie, 27, was a one-year starter at Penn State. He was a second-team All-American and a first-team All-Big 10 selection as a senior. The Falcons used the No. 38 overall pick on him in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft.  
 Ebiketie played out the final year of his four-year, $8,818,664 contract that included a $3,593,574 signing bonus. He was testing the open market as an unrestricted free agent for the first time in his NFL career when he signed a one-year deal with the Eagles that included $4.3 million guaranteed. 
 In 2026, Ebiketie has appeared in nine games for the Eagles and recorded 25 total tackles and no sacks.
